messages.subject: Compliation process slows down
parts:
Hey everyone, 

I am trying to run a simulation study on N-mixture models. Below is my R code:

library(nimble)
require(coda)
require(mcmcplots)

# Simulation loop to access the performance of the model-based priors.
for (i in 1:S) {
  print(i)
  
  # Simulate some  data with seed fixed 
  set.seed(numebers[i])
  BC = matrix(NA, nrow = M, ncol = J) # matrix to contain the obs. data
  
  # Generate local abudance data (the truth)
  N = rpois(n=M, lambda = lambda)
  
  # conduct repeated measurements (generated replicated counts)
  for (j in 1:J) {
    BC[,j] = rbinom(n=M, size = N, prob = p)
  }
  
  
  # Nimble model
  win.data = list(C = BC, M= nrow(BC), J = ncol(BC))
  
  # Specify model in BUGS language:
  N_mixcode <- nimbleCode( {
    
    # Priors
    lambda ~ dgamma(0.01, 0.01)
    p ~ dbeta(0.5,0.5)
    
    # Likelihood
    # Ecological model for true abundance
    for (i in 1:M) {
      
      N[i] ~ dpois(lambda)      # State model
      
      # Observation model for replicated counts
      for (j in 1:J) {
        C[i,j] ~ dbin(p, N[i]) # Observation model
      }
    }
    
    Ntotal <- sum(N[1:M])       # Total population size at M sites combined
    
    
  })
  
  Nst <- apply(BC, 1, max)+1       # Avoid data/model/inits conflict
  
  # Using model priors 
  
  model_prior = nimbleModel(N_mixcode, constants = win.data, inits = list(N = Nst, lambda =runif(1,1,10), p = runif(1,0,1)))
  cmodel_prior <- compileNimble(model_prior) 
  model_priorconf = configureMCMC(model_prior) 
  model_priorconf$monitors
  model_priorconf$addMonitors(c("Ntotal", "lambda", "p"))
  
  model_prior_mcmc = buildMCMC(model_priorconf)
  model_prior_mod = compileNimble(model_prior_mcmc, project = model_prior, resetFunctions = TRUE)
  model_prior_mcmc.out = runMCMC(model_prior_mod, niter = 35000,  nburnin = 3000, thin = 10, samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE, nchains = 2,  summary = TRUE)
  
  model_p[i,] = model_prior_mcmc.out$summary$all.chains[c('p'),]
  model_lambda[i,] = model_prior_mcmc.out$summary$all.chains[c('lambda'),]
  model_Ntotal[i,] = model_prior_mcmc.out$summary$all.chains[c('Ntotal'),]  
  true_N[i,]= sum(N)
  p_eff[i,] = effectiveSize(model_prior_mcmc.out$samples[,c('p')])
  lam_eff[i,] = effectiveSize(model_prior_mcmc.out$samples[,c('lambda')])
  Ntotal_eff[i,] = effectiveSize(model_prior_mcmc.out$samples[,c('Ntotal')])
  prhat = gelman.diag(model_prior_mcmc.out$samples[,c('Ntotal', 'lambda','p')]) 
  converge[i,]=  prhat$psrf[,1] # parameters seems to converge
  
}

I am aiming for S =250 simulation runs but the concern I am having is that for the 1st 50 or so runs, the compilation time seems normal but as the number of simulation runs increases the compilation time slows down. Most time is spent at  model_prior_mod = compileNimble(model_prior_mcmc, project = model_prior, resetFunctions = TRUE) .  Any suggestions or guidelines on how I can avoid such slow compilation times?

Many thanks  for the help,
Fabian.

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Re: Compliation process slows down
parts:
Fabian,
Any of the NIMBLE developers can jump in here, but I think you don't need to recompile the model for each simulations, if the model dimensions are not changing. So, you could move outside the loop any operations that does not depend on i (e.g., the nimble code, etc), and then inside the loop do something like:


 if(i==1){
model_prior = nimbleModel(N_mixcode, constants = win.data, inits = list(N = Nst, lambda =runif(1,1,10), p = runif(1,0,1)))

model_priorconf = configureMCMC(model_prior)
 model_priorconf$monitors
 model_priorconf$addMonitors(c("Ntotal", "lambda", "p"))
 
 model_prior_mcmc = buildMCMC(model_priorconf)

cmodel_prior <- compileNimble(model_prior)
 model_prior_mod = compileNimble(model_prior_mcmc, project = model_prior, resetFunctions = TRUE)
  }else{
 cmodel_prior$setData(win.data)
  }

Hope that helps,
Glenn

messages.subject: Re: Compliation process slows down
parts:
Glenn, thanks for jumping in here.

Yes, Glann is totally right.  You can build and compile the model and the MCMC once, in advance.
Then, inside your simulations loop, generate new data on each loop iteration, store it into the *compiled* model object, and you can also use new initial values for the MCMC chain by putting them into the model.  Then execute the compiled MCMC, and extract samples for that particular simulation.

Does that make sense?

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Compliation process slows down
parts:
Yes, that's correct.  Thanks for the question Fabian and good answer Glenn.

You can modify data values but not constants after compiling the model.  When both are provided together as "constants" to nimbleModel, nimble decides which are which.

A technical details is that model$setData is intended mostly for the uncompiled model before MCMC configuration, because it not only sets the values but also flags which nodes are considered data for purposes of configuring the MCMC.  If you use compiled_model$setData as suggested, it's ok because it will modify the values of the data nodes, but it won't (can't) modify which nodes are flagged as data because the MCMC has already been set up.  For that reason, we consider it slightly better style to modify desired values at that step simply by

cmodel_prior$C <- your_new_C

However using setData will have the convenience of handling multiple data variables if needed.

The slowdown you are seeing may be the result of high memory use.  If you have a need to repeatedly compile, you can try nimble:::clearCompiled(cmodel_prior) after you are done with each one. It should clear everything related to that project, including the compiled MCMC.  The end of the User Manual also has a couple of options for reducing memory use.

-Perry
